body:
Fixes #5988.

`get<T>()` of a JSON boolean in `basic_json` returns 0/1 for arithmetic types but throws `type_error.302` for exactly `number_integer_t`, `number_unsigned_t` and `number_float_t` (their dedicated `from_json()` overloads go through `get_arithmetic_value()`, which has no boolean case). This has been the behaviour of all 3.x releases and stays unchanged. `json_view::get<T>()` returned 0/1 for every `T`, contradicting its documented parity with `basic_json`.

### Changes

- `detail/view/value.hpp`: a trait `rejects_boolean<T, BasicJsonType>` (true for exactly the three number types of the view's `BasicJsonType`, so custom specializations are followed) selects, by tag dispatch, between 0/1 and the same `type_error.302` the DOM throws, with the view's usual path/bytes decoration. `get_to()` and `value()` follow because they go through `get<T>()`.
- Docs: `basic_json/get.md` gets a note "Booleans as numbers" describing the matrix; `basic_json_view/get.md` names the three exceptions.
- Tests: `unit-conversions1.cpp` pins the DOM matrix (portable types only: `long`/`unsigned long` are `int64_t`/`uint64_t` on some platforms); `unit-json_view.cpp` compares DOM and view (same value or the same exception message) for true/false over 17 arithmetic types, plus `get_to()` and `value()`. The view test fails on develop and passes with the fix.

### Performance

A/B harness (`view_iterate`, Mac instruction counts), develop → this PR: walk 0.997–1.001, items 1.002–1.008, get canada 0.992, lookup twitter 1.001. No row worse than 1 %.

### Public API

No breaking changes for `basic_json`. `json_view` (unreleased) now throws `type_error.302` for `get<std::int64_t>()`, `get<std::uint64_t>()` and `get<double>()` (with the default types) of a boolean, as `basic_json` does.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### Performance check

**Neutral to slightly positive.** Only `arithmetic_value<T>()` changes, and only its boolean branch, which now calls a `[[noreturn]]` throw helper for the three exact number types.

- **Generated code** (clang, arm64): the only function that differs in the whole benchmark binary is the loop calling `json_view::get<std::int64_t>()` (`view_ints`). It is **one 16-byte block shorter**. Every other function is identical, including `dump()`, `==` and the builder.
- **Instruction counts**:

| case | base instr/rep | PR instr/rep | PR/base |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `get<std::int64_t>()` over small_signed_ints | 19.02 M | 17.51 M | **0.9203** |
| `json_document` parse twitter | 3.02 M | 3.02 M | 0.9997 |
| view `dump()` canada | 31.13 M | 31.12 M | 0.9998 |
| view `==` json, twitter | 5.82 M | 5.84 M | 1.0036 |

  Timed on the Mac, the `get<std::int64_t>()` loop is 0.4 % faster: 0.9956 geomean, all 4 code layouts below 1. Time moves much less than instructions here. The `==` row is noise, since its machine code is identical.

<details><summary>Method</summary>

- PR head vs. its base (merge base), both compiled into one binary (namespaces renamed per copy) with the same workload: DOM parse (string, stream, callback), copy/destroy, `==`/`<`, iteration, `dump()`, msgpack/UBJSON/BJData read and write, `json_document` parse/`dump()`/`==`/`get<std::int64_t>()` on twitter, citm_catalog, canada and small_signed_ints.
- **Generated code**: both variants disassembled (Apple clang 21, `-O3`, arm64), names and addresses masked, compared function by function.
- **Instruction counts**: Apple M1 Max, instructions retired per repetition (minimum of 3 runs, setup subtracted). Rows whose machine code is identical vary by about ±0.4 %, which is the noise floor. Where a hot path changes, also GCC 13.3 `-O3` on x86-64 under callgrind, which gives exact counts (built with `-falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64` unless a row says otherwise).
</details>

---

linked_issues.body:
### Description

Whether `get<T>()` of a JSON **boolean** yields `0`/`1` or throws depends on which arithmetic `T` is asked for, and `json_view::get<T>()` disagrees with `basic_json::get<T>()` for exactly the types where the DOM throws:

| `T` | `json(true).get<T>()` | `json_document::parse("true").root().get<T>()` |
|---|---|---|
| `int`, `long`, `unsigned`, `short`, `char`, `float`, `long double` | 1 | 1 |
| `long long` / `std::int64_t` (`number_integer_t`), `std::uint64_t` (`number_unsigned_t`), `double` (`number_float_t`) | throws `[json.exception.type_error.302] type must be number, but is boolean` | 1 |

(`get<bool>()` gives `true` in both.) So `get<int>()` and `get<long long>()` of the same value behave differently, and `get<float>()` works while `get<double>()` throws.

**Root cause (DOM).** [from_json.hpp](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/blob/ddc34f546a652cd098dd78225d80f1909b921871/include/nlohmann/detail/conversions/from_json.hpp) has dedicated overloads for `number_float_t`, `number_unsigned_t` and `number_integer_t` ([#L240-L256](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/blob/ddc34f546a652cd098dd78225d80f1909b921871/include/nlohmann/detail/conversions/from_json.hpp#L240-L256)) that call `get_arithmetic_value()`, which has no `boolean` case and throws `type_error.302` ([#L194-L199](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/blob/ddc34f546a652cd098dd78225d80f1909b921871/include/nlohmann/detail/conversions/from_json.hpp#L194-L199)); every other arithmetic type takes the generic overload at [#L611-L625](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/blob/ddc34f546a652cd098dd78225d80f1909b921871/include/nlohmann/detail/conversions/from_json.hpp#L611-L625), whose comment says *"unlike get_arithmetic_value(), a boolean is accepted here"*. The split is old: 3.11.3 and 3.12.0 behave the same (checked with the 3.12.0 single header), and #5902 (2026-10-25) preserved it. Neither [`get()`](https://json.nlohmann.me/api/basic_json/get/) nor the number-handling docs mention how booleans convert, and no test pins the current matrix.

**Root cause (json_view).** `arithmetic_value()` in [view/value.hpp#L41-L63](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/blob/ddc34f546a652cd098dd78225d80f1909b921871/include/nlohmann/detail/view/value.hpp#L41-L63) returns `0`/`1` for a boolean for every arithmetic `T`. The view's documentation ([basic_json_view/get.md](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/blob/ddc34f546a652cd098dd78225d80f1909b921871/docs/mkdocs/docs/api/basic_json_view/get.md), lines 12-13) says *"arithmetic types other than bool (for a boolean, 0/1, exactly as for BasicJsonType::get<T>())"* and that it throws *"the same exception, with the same message, that BasicJsonType::get<T>() throws for the same JSON type and T"*. Both statements are false for `double`, `long long`, `std::int64_t` and `std::uint64_t`. (`#5923`/`#5974` added these promises.)

**Since when.** DOM inconsistency: all of 3.x (verified in 3.12.0). json_view disagreement: develop only (json_view is unreleased).

**Possible fix.** Decide one behaviour for the DOM:

- either make the three exact-type overloads accept a boolean too (add the `boolean` case to `get_arithmetic_value()`, or route the exact types through the generic overload) — silently changes code that today relies on the throw;
- or make the generic overload throw for booleans as well — breaks code that today reads `get<int>()` from a boolean.

Either is a behaviour change, so per the project's rule it belongs behind an opt-in macro with the 3.x default, or the current matrix is documented in `get.md` and tested. Independently of that, the view must match the DOM: either `arithmetic_value()` throws `type_error.302` for `number_float_t`/`number_integer_t`/`number_unsigned_t` or the view documentation stops claiming parity. A test comparing `get<T>()` of a boolean for the full list of arithmetic types between `json` and `json_view` would keep the two in step.

### Reproduction steps

1. Save the program below as `boolconv.cpp`.
2. `clang++ -std=c++17 -I include boolconv.cpp -o boolconv && ./boolconv`

### Expected vs. actual results

Expected: one column of identical answers (all `1` or all throwing), and both columns equal.

Actual: see the table above / the output below.

### Minimal code example

```cpp
#include <nlohmann/json_view.hpp>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdint>
using json = nlohmann::json;
template<class T> void row(const char* name)
{
    json j = true; auto d = nlohmann::json_document::parse("true");
    std::string a, b;
    try { a = std::to_string(static_cast<double>(j.get<T>())); } catch (const json::exception& e) { a = e.what(); }
    try { b = std::to_string(static_cast<double>(d.root().get<T>())); } catch (const json::exception& e) { b = e.what(); }
    std::printf("get<%-12s> dom: %-70s view: %s\n", name, a.c_str(), b.c_str());
}
int main()
{
    row<int>("int"); row<long>("long"); row<long long>("long long"); row<std::int64_t>("int64_t"); row<std::uint64_t>("uint64_t");
    row<unsigned>("unsigned"); row<short>("short"); row<char>("char"); row<float>("float"); row<double>("double"); row<long double>("long double");
}
```

### Error messages

```
get<int         > dom: 1.000000                                                               view: 1.000000
get<long        > dom: 1.000000                                                               view: 1.000000
get<long long   > dom: [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be number, but is boolean    view: 1.000000
get<int64_t     > dom: [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be number, but is boolean    view: 1.000000
get<uint64_t    > dom: [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be number, but is boolean    view: 1.000000
get<unsigned    > dom: 1.000000                                                               view: 1.000000
get<short       > dom: 1.000000                                                               view: 1.000000
get<char        > dom: 1.000000                                                               view: 1.000000
get<float       > dom: 1.000000                                                               view: 1.000000
get<double      > dom: [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be number, but is boolean    view: 1.000000
get<long double > dom: 1.000000                                                               view: 1.000000
```

### Compiler and operating system

Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2), macOS 27 (`long` is 64-bit but a distinct type from `long long`, hence the `long` row).

### Library version

develop at ddc34f546a (2026-11-01); the DOM part also in 3.12.0.

### Validation

- [x] The bug also occurs if the latest version from the [`develop`](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/tree/develop) branch is used.
- [x] I can successfully [compile and run the unit tests](https://github.com/nlohmann/json#execute-unit-tests).

---
*Found by a json_view-vs-DOM differential test during a bug hunt; written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.*
